description:
Blackcomb is a web browser for Mac, iPhone and iPad, built on WebKit, the engine Safari uses. It keeps your pages on your device and does a few things Safari does not.

Float (Mac). Shift-Command-F pops the current page into a small window that stays above every app on every Space. Make it see-through, or let clicks pass through it to what is underneath.

Pair (iPhone and iPad). Two pages in one window, side by side or stacked, each with its own address bar.

Reading list. Save a page and its text stays on the device. Read it later without a connection, at your own text size, or have it read aloud.

Site rules. Per-site zoom, a dark look, and blocking of images, scripts or pop-ups.

Automation (Mac). Off by default. Turn it on and an AI agent on your Mac can open pages, read them, click and type, over a local connection that needs a token and never sees private tabs.

Everything you expect is there too: a start page with your favorites and recent sites, suggestions from your own bookmarks and history as you type, downloads, tabs and private tabs, find in page, tracker blocking, and one step to close every tab and clear your data.

No account, no analytics, no ads. Your history and bookmarks never leave the device.
whatsNew:
Downloads: files go to your Downloads folder, with a list in the toolbar.
The address bar suggests your own bookmarks and history as you type.
A start page with your favorites, Google first, and each site's own icon.
Close Tabs and Clear Data closes every tab and clears history, cookies and site data in one step.
Reopen Closed Tab, Command-1 to 9, Control-Tab, and per-site zoom with Command plus and minus.
The address bar now sits in the title bar.
promotionalText: A WebKit browser with a reading list that works offline, a page that floats above every app, and per-site rules.
